strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with loop-fused scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all_reduce calls with local scaling operations fused into tight loops between each collective. Expected 8 all_reduce dispatches plus local compute. This is the baseline reference approach that prioritizes simplicity and minimal intermediate buffering, trading off potential overlapping opportunities for straightforward sequencing.

strategies.name: Batched all-reduce with pre-computed scale tensors
strategies.desc: Pre-computes all scaling coefficient tensors (a[r], 1/a[r], a[r]/W) as broadcast-ready views, then executes 8 all_reduce operations using vectorized element-wise ops instead of explicit loops. Expected 8 all_reduce dispatches with reduced host-device synchronization overhead. Trades memory for fewer kernel launches by materializing scale patterns once.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter followed by all-gather chain
strategies.desc: Replaces each all_reduce with a reduce_scatter + all_gather pair, allowing each rank to compute its shard-specific scaling only on local data between the two primitives. Expected 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but with smaller per-rank payloads (1024 vs 224*1024 elements) during the reduce_scatter phase, exploiting the fact that scaling is shard-local.

strategies.name: Pipelined dual-buffer all-reduce stages
strategies.desc: Uses two rotating buffers to enable overlapping of the next stage's local scaling computation with the current stage's all_reduce collective, issuing non-blocking all_reduce calls where possible. Expected 8 all_reduce dispatches with potential latency hiding through double-buffering, trading memory footprint for reduced critical path length in the dependency chain.

strategies.name: Hierarchical all-reduce with intra-node fusion
strategies.desc:
Exploits multi-node topology by first performing intra-node all_reduce operations (reducing from 224 ranks to node-level aggregates), applying scaling transformations at node granularity, then performing inter-node all_reduce to finalize. Expected ~16 collective dispatches (8 stages × 2 levels) but with dramatically reduced inter-node bandwidth consumption by moving scaling logic between hierarchy levels.
